messages:
Sara (Support): FYI - ACME hit a major p99 spike and a flurry of 502/401s around 15:03 UTC. Customer is unhappy, raising an incident.
Zoe (Eng-SRE): details? logs?
Sara (Support): sent logs to the thread, gist: https://go/acme-p99-logs - pattern: lots of small prompts, auth refresh failures, then big tail latency.
Ryan (Eng-Platform): @Zoe can you paste the sampling of request headers? wondering if tenant auth TTL + refresh churn is interacting with the coalescer.
Sara (Support): snippet from request stream: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <short-lived-token>
Content-Length: 132
```
and lots of 401s followed by retries from their client.
Miguel (Oncall): ops-bot, any infra alerts?
ops-bot: [alert] host-gpu-21 p95 latency > 800ms for /v1/generate (15:02 - 15:06 UTC). Autoscaler unchanged.
Zoe (Eng-SRE): reading logs — many requests with tiny payloads queued into the continuous batcher. When auth refresh fails the client retries, generating duplicate inflight tokens; coalescer holds tiny requests waiting for batch full or timeout. Head-of-line blocked by a few requests waiting on auth handshake => tail spike.
Ryan (Eng-Platform): that's consistent with the metric: batch_hold_time median increased from 6ms -> 48ms, skewed by holdouts from auth retries.
Zoe (Eng-SRE): repro plan: simulate 200 concurrent tiny prompts with intermittent 401 from auth server to mimic token refresh flapping.
Sara (Support): can reproduce locally with this loop: 
```
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' &
done
```
Then kill token refresh endpoint for ~10s.
Miguel (Oncall): immediate mitigation for customer: disable coalescing for their tenant (per-tenant override) and set max_wait_ms=8. That should reduce head-of-line waiting.
Zoe (Eng-SRE): agree. Also patch batcher to check auth status earlier: if token refresh in-progress for that tenant, don't include other requests behind it (avoid headlock). Short-term hotfix: add tenant-level bypass when auth error rate > 2% for 1m.
Ryan (Eng-Platform): I'll push a canary: set tenant.override.coalesce=false for ACME on dedicated router and roll to 10% of their traffic now.
support-bot: applied override for tenant acme-prod -> coalesce:false (canary 10%).
Sara (Support): customer confirmed immediate p99 drop from ~1.6s -> ~220ms on canary subset. They're asking for permanent fix.
Zoe (Eng-SRE): followups: 1) add a metric to surface tenant auth-refresh-rate, 2) implement short-circuit in batcher to avoid grouping requests behind auth failures, 3) document recommended client behavior (exponential backoff before retrying auth to avoid retry storms).
Miguel (Oncall): escalation notes for postmortem: timeline, root cause (auth TTL/refresh churn + continuous coalescing head-of-line), mitigations applied (tenant coalesce off, short-circuit), customer impact. I'll file incident and schedule 1hr postmortem.
Ryan (Eng-Platform): deployment plan for proper fix: small batcher patch + feature flag rollout, then migrate tenant override to automatic detection when auth refresh anomalies detected. I'll open PR and tag for review.
Zoe (Eng-SRE): quick config suggestion for ops until fix: lower default max_wait_ms from 24 -> 12 for small-payload routes, and enable tenant auth anomaly detector.
Sara (Support): forwarding this to ACME CSM and CISO. They want root cause and timeline for full fix.
Zoe (Eng-SRE): I'll write the incident blurb and include repro steps above + logs.
Miguel (Oncall): marking as active incident. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
